conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're inquiring about your son Alex, who is 8 years old.

Let me ask you a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex:

**Does Alex live with you, or if he doesn't live with you, are you contributing at least the same amount as Child Benefit would pay (or the equivalent in kind) towards his care - for example, on food, clothes or pocket money?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't live with me currently. As for what I contribute towards his care... I'm not entirely sure if what I'm giving him is equal to the Child Benefit rate or not. I do try to help out when I can, but I don't know the exact amount that Child Benefit pays.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Let me help clarify this for you.

Child Benefit currently pays £25.60 per week for the eldest or only child, and £16.95 per week for each additional child. So for Alex as your only child (or eldest), that would be £25.60 per week, which works out to approximately £110-111 per month.

The contributions can include things like:
- Money you give directly
- Clothes you buy for him
- Food you provide
- Pocket money
- Presents
- Financial contributions toward providing him with somewhere to live

These contributions can be made weekly, monthly, or even as a lump sum to cover a set period.

**Can you tell me approximately how much you contribute toward Alex's care each week or month when you add up all these types of support?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm really not sure, to be honest. Some weeks I might help out with a few things, other weeks less so. I don't keep a running total of what I'm spending on him. Is it important to know the exact amount?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, it is quite important for determining your eligibility, and here's why:

Since Alex doesn't live with you, the key rule is that you can still qualify for Child Benefit **if you're contributing at least the same amount as Child Benefit pays** (which is approximately £25.60 per week or £110-111 per month) towards his upkeep.

Without being able to confirm that you're meeting this contribution threshold, I cannot definitively determine whether you would be eligible.

Let me ask you this: **Who does Alex currently live with? Is someone else claiming Child Benefit for him?**

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at a time.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with his mum. I'm not sure if she's already claiming Child Benefit for him or not.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. This is an important piece of information.

Here's the situation: **Only one person can claim Child Benefit for Alex at any given time.** If his mum is already claiming Child Benefit for him, then you would not be able to claim it simultaneously.

Let me ask: **Do you know whether Alex's mum is currently claiming Child Benefit for him?** 

If you're not certain, that's okay - I just need to understand your situation fully to give you an accurate assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I honestly don't know if she's claiming it or not. We don't really discuss those sorts of things.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Thank you for being honest about what you know and don't know.

Let me ask one more question to complete my assessment:

**Is Alex in any special circumstances, such as being in hospital, in care, or living in residential accommodation for an extended period? Or is he living normally at home with his mum?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nothing like that. He's just living normally at home with his mum.
